replies.text: {"verdicts":[{"id":"T1","keep":true,"reason":"Design puts API key in query string; log/Referer leakage of permanent credential is concrete and supported."},{"id":"T2","keep":true,"reason":"Design explicitly states keys never expire; unbounded impersonation window with no revocation is a distinct lifecycle attack."},{"id":"T3","keep":true,"reason":"No rate limiting plus public API and PII access supports bulk harvesting/key-spraying attack."},{"id":"T4","keep":true,"reason":"Quote shows single key grants all orders and customer emails; lack of scoping blast radius is supported."},{"id":"T5","keep":true,"reason":"Public internet-facing API with no rate limiting supports resource-exhaustion denial of service for other partners."},{"id":"T6","keep":false,"reason":"Quotes state keys are scoped to the partner's own orders; missing per-object ownership check is not in the design."},{"id":"T7","keep":true,"reason":"Permanent per-partner key plausibly shared; attribution gap during PII export is a concrete distinct harm."}]}
